title: Garmenting (ready-made garments)
subtitle: A newer, growing segment turning Surat fabric into garments
covers: This page covers ready-made garment units in Surat. It is a newer segment than weaving or processing, so public data is thin.

snapshot.text: Surat's garment sector was reported at about 1 crore garments a month and about Rs 600 crore monthly turnover, mainly man-made fibre and denim (Nov 2025).
A Surat manufacturer said garments offer better value and timely payments compared with fabric, where payment delays are an issue.
Gujarat Textile Policy 2024 gives garments its highest support ('Activity 1'): capital subsidy up to 35% and payroll assistance of Rs 4,000-5,000 per worker a month for Gujarat-domicile EPF workers.

items.text: A garment unit cuts and stitches fabric into finished clothing, adds trims and packs it for brands, retailers or wholesale buyers.
New garment hubs: Hojiwala, Sachin, Pandesara and especially the BRC Industrial Estate in Udhna.
An ISID study (Mar 2026) notes emerging garment manufacturing as one of the forces slowly formalising Surat's largely informal cluster.

items.text: Public fabric quotes exist only for grey fabric (see the weaving page). Garment makers buy finished fabric, so use the customer's purchase bills.

Brands and organised retailers often ask for social-compliance audits; ask which audits the unit holds. Pollution category depends on whether the unit washes, dyes or prints; plain cut-and-sew is usually low-polluting, but confirm with GPCB papers.
Payroll assistance under Gujarat Textile Policy 2024 applies only to Gujarat-domicile workers registered under EPF.
Labour is largely migrant. About 30% of migrant workers reportedly did not return after the 2024 election and wedding season, and some units stopped night shifts.

Power: GERC's FY2025-26 DGVCL tariff schedule lists the Non-RGP rate (loads up to 40 kW) at 435 paise a unit up to 10 kW and 465 paise above 10 kW, plus fixed charges and 45 paise extra in peak hours. Larger loads fall in other categories. A new FY2026-27 order was issued on 25 Mar 2026, so confirm current rates from the customer's bills.

sections.title: Fragility points and early warning signs for a lender

items.text: Buyer concentration: one large brand order can be most of the business; a lost order hits hard.
Fashion and returns risk: unsold or rejected goods. Ask about rejection and return rates.
Subsidy-led investment: projects that only work with subsidy are fragile if the subsidy is delayed. Do not count unsanctioned subsidy as income.
Cheque returns or frequent overdraws; cash credit used near the limit all month.
Electricity units falling month on month, or a shift stopped, without a matching fall in loan outstanding.
Creditor days stretching; suppliers charging late-payment interest; purchases switched to cash from new sources.
Stock or receivables building up; sales concentrated on one or two parties or brokers.
Wages paid late or labour leaving; regular weekly closures.
New borrowing from private lenders or related parties; machines rented out or sold.
